newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - West German prelim Aug CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - West German prelim Aug CPI.

text.p: Following are comments from economists after the German Federal Statistics Office said west German August preliminary CPI was down 0.1 percent month-on-month, up 1.4 percent year-on-year.
Gerhard Grebe, chief economist at Bank Julius Baer:

"The monthly figure is what we expected, we corrected it slightly upwards on Friday. The annual figure 1.4 percent is not unusual for August. This is a favourable figure, but the next rates will be higher -- we have seen the lowest rates.
"For the year-end for the whole of Germany we are forecasting a rate of 1.8 percent."
Mathias Haffner, economist at BZW, Frankfurt:

"The figures are basically positive. They could be reduced still further to zero when the other states (whose data are not used in compiling the provisional West German figures) come in. But that makes no fundamental difference and in the medium term we see the outlook as continuing positive."
"The rate of 1.4 percent fits in with our expectations and will be viewed positively. For 1996 we have a year-end forecast of 1.5 percent, and if we reach that it will have a stabilising effect."
